input:
/data/legacy holds text files in mixed encodings. For every file whose name ends in `.txt` (case-sensitive), write a normalised copy with the same name to /out/clean/: UTF-8 without BOM, line endings 
 and lone  converted to 
, and ending with exactly one added 
 if the text did not already end with 
.
Detect each file's encoding in this order: starts with a UTF-16 BOM (FF FE or FE FF) -> utf-16; starts with the UTF-8 BOM -> utf-8-sig; decodes as UTF-8 -> utf-8 (plain ASCII included); otherwise latin-1.
Write /out/manifest.tsv (tab-separated, header name, encoding, lines, chars) with one row per file sorted by name, where lines is the number of 
 and chars the number of Unicode characters in the normalised text (newlines included, BOM excluded).

transcript.final_response:
I've written cleaned copies of the six `.txt` files to `/out/clean/` and created `/out/manifest.tsv`. I checked the bytes of every output file: they're all UTF-8 with no BOM, contain only `\n` line endings, and end with exactly one newline.

`/out/manifest.tsv`:
```
name	encoding	lines	chars
a.txt	utf-8	2	24
b.txt	utf-8-sig	2	26
c.txt	latin-1	2	23
d.txt	utf-16	3	16
e.txt	utf-8	2	30
f.txt	latin-1	3	17
```

What was done to each file:
- **a.txt:** already clean UTF-8, copied unchanged.
- **b.txt:** removed the UTF-8 BOM and converted `\r\n` to `\n`.
- **c.txt:** isn't valid UTF-8, so it was read as latin-1 ("Señor Müller", "À bientôt"). Added a final `\n`.
- **d.txt:** UTF-16 with a byte-order mark ("Ωmega", "κόσμε", "end"). Converted `\r\n` to `\n`.
- **e.txt:** plain ASCII, so it counts as utf-8. Added a final `\n`.
- **f.txt:** used old Mac-style lone `\r` line endings, which became `\n`. It was read as latin-1 because of a `£` byte.

`g.TXT` was skipped because only lowercase `.txt` names count, so it isn't in `/out/clean/` or the manifest.
tool_calls: ls -la /data/legacy; cd /data/legacy && for f in *; do echo "== $f"; head -c 64 "$f" | od -c | head -5; done

mkdir -p /out/clean && python3 - <<'EOF'
import os
src='/data/legacy'; rows=[]
for name in sorted(os.listdir(src)):
    p=os.path.join(src,name)
    if not name.endswith('.txt') or not os.path.isfile(p): continue
    b=open(p,'rb').read()
    if b[:2] in (b'\xff\xfe',b'\xfe\xff'): enc='utf-16'
    elif b[:3]==b'\xef\xbb\xbf': enc='utf-8-sig'
    else:
        try: b.decode('utf-8'); enc='utf-8'
        except UnicodeDecodeError: enc='latin-1'
    t=b.decode(enc)
    if t.startswith('\ufeff'): t=t[1:]
    t=t.replace('\r\n','\n').replace('\r','\n')
    if not t.endswith('\n'): t+='\n'
    open(os.path.join('/out/clean',name),'w',encoding='utf-8',newline='').write(t)
    rows.append((name,enc,t.count('\n'),len(t)))
with open('/out/manifest.tsv','w',newline='') as f:
    f.write('name\tencoding\tlines\tchars\n')
    for r in rows: f.write('\t'.join(map(str,r))+'\n')
EOF
cat /out/manifest.tsv; for f in /out/clean/*; do echo "== $f"; od -c "$f"|head -4; done
